o.text: From Proto-Turkic *adï- (“to separate”), whence also ayrı (“separate, different”) and ayrılmaq (“to separate, break up”). Cognate with Turkish ayırmak; see there for more.

Borrowed from Classical Persian مُژْدَه (mužda, “good news”), from Parthian 𐫖𐫇𐫋𐫅𐫃 (mwjdg /⁠muždag⁠/, “(good) news, message”), from Proto-Iranian *miždám, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *miždʰám, from Proto-Indo-European *misdʰós. Related to Classical Persian مُزْد (muzd).
A derivation of Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ. By surface analysis, öz + -ək.
Borrowed from Russian ре́квием (rékvijem), from Latin requiem.
